content.summary: Welcome to B1 Reading Mission 02. In this lesson, you will read short stories about people looking back at past choices and thinking about how things could have been different. You will learn how to use the third conditional to talk about imaginary past situations, regrets, and alternative outcomes.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Third Conditional structures using If + had + past participle, followed by would have + past participle.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to making decisions, evaluating consequences, and reflecting on past opportunities.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming texts for general emotional tone and scanning for specific details about past events and their results.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short B1 texts about past mistakes and alternative choices.
Locate specific details regarding cause and effect in past scenarios.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with the third conditional in reading passages.

contextWarmup.prompt: What do people usually talk about when they use the third conditional?
options: Things that happened differently in the past and cannot be changed
General facts and scientific truths about the world

contextWarmup.explanation: The third conditional is specifically used to imagine past situations that did not happen and think about their alternative results.

rules: Pola dasar: If + Subject + had + V3 (Past Participle), Subject + would have + V3. Contoh: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
Klausa 'if' menggunakan Past Perfect (had + V3) untuk menunjukkan kondisi masa lalu yang tidak terpenuhi. Klausa hasil menggunakan would/could/might + have + V3.
Urutan klausa bisa dibalik: She would have arrived on time if she had left earlier. Jika klausa 'if' di tengah, tidak perlu koma.
Kontraksi alami dalam percakapan: would've = would have, could've = could have, should've = should have, hadn't = had not. Contoh: If you'd called me, I would've helped you.
Gunakan 'could have' untuk kemungkinan atau kemampuan masa lalu: If he had trained more, he could have won the competition. Gunakan 'might have' untuk kemungkinan yang lebih rendah.

commonTrap.explanation: Students often put 'would have' inside the 'if' clause by mistake. Remember that 'would have' only belongs in the main clause.
commonTrap.wrong: If I would have known about the meeting, I would have attended.
commonTrap.correct: If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.

content.passageTitle: Looking Back: The Road Not Taken
paragraphs: Yesterday evening, Mark sat by his window and stared at an old photograph from his university days. He often thought about how different his life would have been if he had chosen a different career path. Ten years ago, he received an offer to study graphic design in London. However, he decided to stay in his hometown and take a safe office job because he was afraid of change.

If he had accepted the London scholarship, he might have become a professional artist and traveled the world. Instead, he stayed behind and never pushed himself out of his comfort zone. Although his current job is stable, he sometimes feels a deep sense of regret. He realizes that if he had taken that risk, he would have experienced countless exciting opportunities and learned valuable life lessons much earlier.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Third Conditional Past Regrets

content.summary: Master the third conditional structure in English to write about alternative past outcomes, missed opportunities, and personal reflections on past mistakes.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: The Basic Formula
blueprintItems.formula: If + Subject + had + past participle, Subject + would have + past participle
blueprintItems.example: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the English exam.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Modal Variations in Results
blueprintItems.formula: If + Subject + had + V3, Subject + could have / might have + V3
blueprintItems.example: If she had left home earlier, she could have caught the morning train.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Clause Order and Commas
blueprintItems.formula: Result clause first (no comma) + If clause
blueprintItems.example: They would have won the match if they had practiced every single day.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma after the if clause when it comes at the beginning of the sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: If you had told me about the meeting I would have attended.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: If you had told me about the meeting, I would have attended.
mechanicsRules.why: A dependent introductory clause requires a comma before the main clause.

mechanicsRules.rule: Never use 'would have' inside the if clause.
mechanicsRules.badExample: If I would have known the truth, I would have stayed home.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: If I had known the truth, I would have stayed home.
mechanicsRules.why: The if clause takes the past perfect tense (had), while the main clause takes would have.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize the first letter of every new sentence and proper names.
mechanicsRules.badExample: if mark had visited london, he would have seen big ben.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: If Mark had visited London, he would have seen Big Ben.
mechanicsRules.why: Standard capitalization rules apply to conditional sentences in paragraphs.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Third Conditional Imagining Alternative Past Outcomes

content.summary: Mastering the third conditional requires smooth weak forms, fast auxiliary reductions like 'had' and 'have', and clear stress on past participles to sound natural.
content.audioGuidance: Pay close attention to how auxiliary verbs contract in rapid speech. For example, 'If you had known' sounds like 'If you'd known', and 'would have' sounds like 'would've'.

pillars.name: Auxiliary Reduction
pillars.target: Reduce 'had' to /əd/ or /d/ and 'have' to /əv/ in connected speech
pillars.explanation: Native speakers rarely stress helper verbs in third conditional sentences. Practicing weak forms helps you maintain a natural conversational rhythm.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.target: Emphasize main verbs and alternative outcomes
pillars.explanation: Place pitch prominence on the condition and the result verbs to highlight the contrast between what actually happened and what you are imagining.

pillars.name: Intonation Contours
pillars.target: Use rising intonation on the if-clause and falling intonation on the result clause
pillars.explanation: This melodic pattern signals to your listener that the condition is complete and the alternative outcome is now being delivered.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The primary stress remains on the second syllable across both the verb and adjective forms.
Notice how compound nouns usually stress the first element, while longer adjectives shift the stress inward.
Adding suffixes shifts the primary stress toward the end of the noun form.
The stress stays firmly on the second syllable even when adding the noun suffix.

writing.explanation: Past perfect 'had taken' is required in the condition, followed by 'wouldn't have gotten' in the result.

targetAnswers: If he had practiced the piano every day, he could have played in the concert.
If he had practiced the piano every day, he could've played in the concert.
writing.explanation: Use 'could have' in the result clause to express an unfulfilled past ability or possibility.

writing.explanation: Change affirmative past simple to negative past perfect in the condition.

practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe an opportunity you missed in the past and how things might have changed.
storyPoints: What the opportunity was and when it happened
Why you failed to take advantage of it
What outcome would have occurred if you had acted differently
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If I had accepted that scholarship, I would have studied abroad in Europe.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Maintain a steady speaking pace and link your clauses smoothly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to your colleague who is regretting a missed business deal last month.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are discussing a failed investment at work with your business partner.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: My partner says: 'I really regret not investing in that tech startup when we had the chance.' How do you reply using a third conditional sentence?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If we had invested in that startup, we would have made a massive profit.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf wi hæd ɪnˈvestɪd ɪn ðæt ˈstɑːtʌp/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Respond naturally in character, using the correct third conditional grammar.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to your teacher who is asking about your exam preparation.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are talking to your professor after receiving a disappointing test score.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your professor says: 'You looked unprepared during the test today.' How do you reply using the third conditional?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If I had prepared more carefully over the weekend, I wouldn't have failed the exam.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Show empathy and accountability using past unreal conditionals.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to your friend who experienced a travel mishap because of bad planning.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You and your friend missed a flight because you left home too late.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your friend says: 'We missed our flight to Bali because we left the house late.' How do you respond?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed our flight.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Keep the conversation engaging and grammatically precise.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to your manager who is questioning a delayed project delivery.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Your team failed to meet the client deadline last Friday.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your manager asks: 'Why did the project fail to launch on time?' How do you explain using the third conditional?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If we had realized the technical bugs sooner, we would have prevented the delay.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf wi hæd ˈrɪəlaɪzd ðə ˈteknɪkl bʌɡz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Explain past causes and hypothetical preventions professionally.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Record a sentence using the target vocabulary word 'alternative' within a third conditional structure.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say a sentence using 'alternative' to describe a past regret.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If we had considered alternative strategies, we wouldn't have lost the contract.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Ensure the target vocabulary word 'alternative' is pronounced clearly with correct stress.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Record a complex third conditional sentence demonstrating inversion of 'had'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say a third conditional sentence starting with 'Had I known...' instead of 'If I had known...'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Had I known about the traffic, I would have taken another route.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Demonstrate advanced grammatical control using auxiliary inversion.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice sentence stress by emphasizing the contrast between the past reality and the imaginary outcome.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Read the target sentence with strong acoustic emphasis on 'would have succeeded'.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If she had worked harder, she WOULD HAVE SUCCEEDED.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf ʃi hæd wɜːkt ˈhɑːdə ʃi wʊd həv səkˈsiːdɪd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Project extra vocal energy and higher pitch on the result clause verbs.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Demonstrate rising intonation on the condition clause and falling intonation on the result clause.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Read the third conditional sentence using the correct rising-falling melodic contour.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If they had asked for help, they would have finished on time.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf ðeɪ hæd ɑːskt fɔː help ðeɪ wʊd həv ˈfɪnɪʃt ɒn taɪm/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a clear pitch rise at the comma pause and a downward glide at the final period.
